Refine the following review experience for the CLAR dimension. Make it concise, actionable, and specific. Focus on common pitfalls and best practices.

Topic: CLAR Review Criteria and Common Weaknesses
Content: When reviewing the CLAR (Clarity) dimension, focus on three sub-dimensions: CLAR-WRT (Writing, Terminology & Algorithm Presentation), CLAR-NOT (Notation & Mathematical Explanation Clarity), and CLAR-FIG (Figures & Visual Aids Clarity). Common weaknesses include: 1) Grammatical errors and awkward phrasing that reduce professionalism (e.g., missing words, sentence fragments). 2) Ambiguous or inconsistent terminology, such as using 'perturbation' for both latent space ($\epsilon$) and image space ($x'-x$) without clear distinction. 3) Inconsistent mathematical notation, such as defining a classifier as $c(\cdot)$ but omitting it in loss functions like $CE(x', y)$ vs $CE(c(x'), y)$. 4) Incomplete experimental setup descriptions that hinder reproducibility, such as missing classifier architecture or training hyperparameters. 5) Unclear figure captions or visual flows that do not align with the text or notation. Constructive suggestions should include specific examples of errors and precise instructions for standardizing notation and terminology.

Return only the refined content.
